brief: Goldman's ETF desk reports over $1.5 trillion has flowed into US ETFs in the first three quarters of 2026, already surpassing 2025's full-year record, running at roughly $167 billion a month and $8 billion a session. Citing that pace plus seasonal Q4 tailwinds, the desk expects full-year flows to exceed $2 trillion. Beyond the headline number, the note catalogs several standalone cross-asset flow and performance observations without tying them into a single thesis. SPX is outperforming RTY for a seventh straight week (longest since 2018) and XLK has outperformed SPX for six weeks, with mega-cap ETF MAGS seeing inflows in 12 of 13 sessions while equal-weight ETF RSP is on a seven-week losing streak. Cybersecurity ETFs are near a best-ever inflow month (+$950mm). TLT hit an all-time low and is on its longest losing streak in two years. Muni bond ETFs are having one of their worst performance months in 20 years yet keep attracting inflows through tax-loss harvesting. Spot-bitcoin ETFs have posted nine straight days of inflows (+$3bn, largest 9-day haul YTD, +$6bn over two months). Rising 10-year yields above 5% have accelerated fixed-income ETF trading volumes.
